articles.title: California voters reject billionaire tax after opponents argued it would harm the economy
articles.summary: A November rally against Proposition 40 at the Iron Workers Apprenticeship Training Center in La Palma. (Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times) California voters have officially rejected the controversial billionaire tax. Proposition 40 sought to impose a one-time 5% tax on California billionaires ’ assets to try to offset federal healthcare funding cuts. Despite the blue wave in the midterm elections, the novel tax on the ultra-wealthy had trailed from the first day of vote counting and was officially rejected on Monday. Roughly 53% of California voters voted against the measure while 47% voted for it,  the Associated Press said as it declared that California voters had rejected the measure. Although the tax was rejected in the vast majority of counties, the final tally showed major pockets of support in Los Angeles and San Francisco — home to the lion’s share of the state’s 200 billionaires. Orange County, however, voted no by a wide margin. Open the interactive version of this graphic The political battle over the ballot measure and two competing proposals divided the state and was among the most expensive in California history.  More than $400 million had been spent on the three intertwined ballot measures, with more than 90% spent opposing the billionaire tax, according to fundraising disclosures filed with the secretary of state’s office. Billionaires, notably Google co-founder Sergey Brin, poured hundreds of millions of dollars into groups that funded ads to kill the billionaire tax. California Gov. Gavin Newsom, the California Teachers Assn. and Planned Parenthood Affiliates of California are among the powerful Democrats and other Democrat-aligned groups that expressed fears that billionaires would flee the state. Some, including Brin and fellow Google co-founder Larry Page, moved out of California because of the proposal. An onslaught of advertisements against the billionaire tax argued it could impact all Californians, not just the ultra-wealthy. Teachers, firefighters and other middle-class Californians became the face of their campaigns, fueling growing opposition ahead of election day. Read more: California’s billionaire tax battle is playing out on Instagram — with paid influencers Opponents of Proposition 40 said Californians made the “right decision,” calling Proposition 40 a “reckless experiment” that would hurt the state’s economy. The group included the California Medical Assn., California Primary Care Assn. and the California School Boards Assn. “Proposition 40 risked California’s economic competitiveness and fiscal stability, as well as the revenue we rely on to fund our top priorities — from education and healthcare to public safety and infrastructure,” the group said. Leaders of the Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West, which sponsored the proposition, vowed to put a billionaire tax proposal on the 2028 ballot if Sacramento leaders don’t find a way to better support the public health sector. Given California’s volatile budget, which is expected to be particularly problematic next year, it appears unlikely that state lawmakers will find a way to backfill an estimated $100 billion of federal healthcare funding cuts. Read more: Billionaire tax continues to trail as many Californians vote to spare the state’s ultra-rich stars Supporters said the proposed tax on more than 200 California billionaires aimed to raise that amount, with 90% funding healthcare, and the remainder going to schools and food assistance. “Billionaire-funded propaganda may have influenced the outcome of this election, but as hospitals reduce services, emergency rooms close and families lose access to care, the truth will become increasingly difficult to hide,” said Suzanne Jimenez, chief of staff for the SEIU-UHW. “Californians will see for themselves what was at stake.” This will not be the end of the debate about taxing the rich. U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Fremont), who both backed Proposition 40, are pushing for the passage of a federal 5% tax on American billionaires. Earlier this year, they introduced the “Make Billionaires Pay Their Fair Share Act.” Despite Democrats winning control of the House and Senate last week, the legislation will probably face constitutional challenges if it passes. articles.title: UFC chief Dana White takes White House podium — but officially turns down Trump
articles.summary: UFC CEO Dana White made his much-discussed visit to the White House on Monday, where he joined U.S. President Donald Trump for a press briefing and officially turned down the president's tongue-in-cheek offer to become his new press secretary. Following a bizarre weekend in which Trump appeared to float the open role of White House press secretary to the UFC boss in a Truth Social post, only to admit a day later that he was "only kidding, but Dana loves the idea,” Trump and White put the discussion to rest to close out a joint press briefing with the two in the nation’s capital. Trump: “So let me ask you the big question. Dana, would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America. Look at the sign — you’d have this behind all the time, ‘The White House, Washington.’ Would you like that or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC?” White: “Thank you for the offer, sir. I do not want to be in politics.” Trump: “I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everyone.” Trump's bizarre press briefing ends with Dana White turning down the press secretary job pic.twitter.com/YACwp3SjXk — Aaron Rupar (@atrupar) November 9, 2026 White briefly took questions from reporters during the press appearance, after which Trump explained how the peculiar situation first arose. “We were having a very bad press day and I don’t know why, I thought of his name,” Trump said. “He’s been a friend for a long time. I said, ‘I think I’m going to get Dana White to be my new press secretary.’ I said it to a group of the press and that was it. I was sort of kidding. “Then they wrote the stories as though I wasn’t kidding, and then [White] was inundated and I was inundated. He was here anyway and we thought we’d have a little fun and we brought Dana here. He would be fantastic.” "The last 24 hours of my life have been insane," White added. White and Trump have maintained a close personal relationship for decades, dating back to the early days of the UFC's rise in the United States, when Trump's Atlantic City hotel and casino hosted two of the promotion's events in 2001. White has since become one of Trump's most prominent supporters in the sports world, speaking at three Republican National Conventions and publicly backing Trump's presidential campaigns. White’s initial reaction to Trump's social media post Saturday only further fueled speculation around his potential appointment. White first posted an image of himself at the podium of the White House press briefing room with the caption, "On to the next chapter," then told reporters in London that he was "flying to Washington" directly after Zuffa Boxing 12's post-fight press conference in order to meet with Trump on Monday. Trump clarified Sunday that his meeting with White was previously scheduled and concerned unrelated matters, which both men reiterated Monday afternoon. In the end, it appears the whole saga ended up being much ado about nothing. articles.title: Trump says he spoke with Nvidia CEO, who denied knowledge of alleged Chinese spy
articles.summary: President Donald Trump stands with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after presenting him with the National Medal of Science in Washington, DC, on October 8. - Evan Vucci/Reuters/FILE President Donald Trump downplayed revelations that close ally and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, insisting Monday that he believed the tech billionaire’s assertion that he knew nothing about the alleged espionage operation . Trump’s dismissal came amid growing scrutiny over the influential role that Huang played in advising Trump on AI and his approach to trade with China, even as the US government’s intelligence agencies scrutinized the suspected spy who grew close to Huang in an investigation that played out for months behind the scenes. “I really believe him,” Trump told reporters during an impromptu White House press conference. “I think that he’ll be in good shape.” The president’s decision to stick by Huang marked the latest development in an extraordinary episode that has raised acute concerns about the economic and national security risks posed by the Nvidia chief’s relationship with the suspected Chinese spy. And it’s likely to deepen Democrats’ concerns over what the White House knew about the conduct of Huang and those around him — and why Trump nevertheless continued to rely heavily on the CEO’s counsel in shaping the nation’s multibillion-dollar artificial intelligence industry. Senior Trump administration officials met earlier Monday with a group of top lawmakers charged with overseeing the nation’s intelligence agencies, during which they discussed the intelligence surrounding Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, an executive at a Singapore-based tech firm who is not related to the Nvidia CEO. The private meeting with the so-called Gang of Eight was initially meant to focus on the war in Iran. But it came days after Jensen Huang admitted to the affair — and nearly a year after the FBI first raised worries to lawmakers that Alice Huang might be feeding information to China, two people familiar with the matter told CNN. (Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Monday that the allegation that Alice Huang was gathering information for Beijing was “purely groundless speculation and an attempt to smear and malign China.”) Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence, and CIA Director John Ratcliffe were spotted on Capitol Hill as Trump officials huddled for more than an hour with the Gang of Eight lawmakers charged with overseeing the nation’s intelligence agencies. But lawmakers indicated afterward they still had more questions than answers, with Democrats vowing a slew of investigations into the matter once they take control of Congress in January. “The export of advanced semiconductors to China or countries where China might access them is a matter of immense national security importance,” Rep. Jim Himes, the top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, said in a statement. “We are aggressively pursuing more information to understand what happened and whether the decision-making process to export chips was improperly influenced or compromised.” Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and built it into one of the world’s most valuable companies, is among a handful of tech billionaires who have played an influential role in shaping Trump’s hands-off regulatory approach to the AI industry. In September, the CEO helped craft a pledge that he and other major AI executives signed at the White House committing to “self-police” their companies. Huang has also repeatedly pressed Trump for greater freedom to sell advanced AI chips to China, putting himself at the center of one of the most critical and contentious debates within the administration. “An amazing man, gotten to know him so well, Jensen Huang,” Trump said last month as he awarded him the National Medal of Science. “The entire world is now running on Nvidia.” Huang’s cozy relationship with Trump, including regular phone calls and trips to Washington for meetings in the West Wing, has persisted despite long-running suspicions within the government that he could be an unwitting conduit of information to China’s government. Federal agents first informed some lawmakers roughly a year ago that they suspected Huang was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort,” citing his close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen who represented the data center company Megaspeed. The FBI officials noted that Alice Huang suddenly had an unusual level of purchasing power for someone in her position, one of the people familiar said. Those initial suspicions formed the foundation of a classified memo issued in May warning that Jensen Huang had a close relationship with a woman the US now concluded was a Chinese spy, a US official and another person familiar with the matter said. The memo was overseen by Secretary of State Marco Rubio and circulated among a small group of senior administration officials before Trump’s trip to China to meet with the country’s leader, Xi Jinping, those sources said. Around the same time, a New York research firm that specializes in betting against publicly traded companies published its own report questioning the “uncomfortably close” relationship between the Nvidia CEO and Alice Huang. Trump did not take any apparent action to distance himself from Jensen Huang. Huang was not initially among the tech executives and businessmen invited to accompany Trump on the China trip, though it’s unclear whether that decision was tied to the Rubio memo. And Trump ultimately insisted that the Nvidia CEO join him. Huang boarded Air Force One during a layover in Alaska, accompanying Trump and his top aides for the final leg of the flight to China. The president later hailed him as “the Great Jensen Huang” in a social media post insisting that reports he was not invited were incorrect. “I will be asking President Xi, a Leader of extraordinary distinction to ‘open up’ China so that these brilliant people can work their magic, and help bring the People’s Republic to an even higher level!” Trump on Monday claimed he only recently learned of the concerns surrounding Huang, and was not aware of the suspected espionage operation when he brought him to Beijing. The revelations have generated far more alarm among federal officials and others in Trump’s orbit, who expressed shock that a suspected Chinese spy could gain such direct access to an executive running perhaps the nation’s most important AI company — and potentially, by extension, decision-making at the government’s highest levels. “Jaw-dropping,” said one former senior Trump official. “The stakes of that are just so high.” Two former senior intelligence officials at the FBI also questioned the decision not to provide Huang with a “defensive briefing” that would have informed him that he could be the target of Chinese intelligence. Some Trump allies, meanwhile, have fretted privately that the question of what the president knew about Huang’s affair, and when, gifted Democrats a potent opportunity to launch damaging investigations — and potentially form the basis for an impeachment effort that many in the president’s orbit have come to see as inevitable after Tuesday’s midterm elections. Senior Democrats in both the House and Senate are already vowing to launch probes into the matter. “The more I learn about the insane relationship between the Trump Administration, Chinese spies, and AI billionaires, the more I’m convinced there is nothing this administration does that isn’t corrupt,” Sen. Chris Coons, who is poised to lead the Senate Foreign Relations Committee next year, wrote in a recent post on X. “Congress will investigate and get answers.” Republicans have also sought information from Nvidia, in a sign of the distress over the prospect of China gaining intelligence that could give it an edge in its intense competition with the US to develop AI technology. A trio of House Republicans last week demanded that Huang sit for a confidential briefing this month. “To me, the real damage goes beyond the attempted influence or the limited intelligence gathering on Nvidia’s [intellectual property] that inevitably occurred,” said Holden Triplett, who served as director of counterintelligence at the National Security Council in the first Trump administration. “It’s all the small details she was likely able to collect about partners, suppliers, how sanctions work in practice, and potential workarounds.” Nvidia said it will conduct its own investigation into Huang’s conduct, though it remains unclear whether the company’s board is willing to fire him — and what repercussions that would have for the economy. There is no obvious successor to Huang, who has turned Nvidia into a powerhouse supplier of the chips at the center of the AI boom. Huang’s troubles have also generated fears throughout the broader sector among lobbyists and policymakers who worry the episode prompted renewed enthusiasm in Congress for more stringently regulating AI companies, dampening the gains that have driven the broader stock market consistently higher. Yet despite the implications for national security, the economy and Trump’s own administration, the president insisted on Monday that none of it much worried him. “I’d certainly check with the intelligence people,” he said of when he was first made aware of the concerns tied to Huang. “They could have been mentioned. Certainly, it didn’t make much of an impact on me.” This story has been updated with additional information. CNN’s Kylie Atwood, Katie Bo Lillis and Sean Lyngaas contributed to this report. articles.title: Trump stands by Hegseth as GOP lawmaker pushes to impeach him
articles.summary: Rep. Thomas Massie, a Republican from Kentucky, reintroduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday, alleging that the embattled Pentagon chief had committed "high crimes and misdemeanors" and abused the power of his office by violating the War Powers Resolution, conducting military operations without congressional authorization and ordering unlawful military actions in several countries. The expected impeachment filing came as Congress returned to Washington, D.C. , to begin a lame-duck session following the historic rout that the GOP suffered in last week's midterm elections . Hegseth is facing intense political backlash over the United States' costly and unpopular war with Iran, which some top Republicans — including  Trump — blame in part for the drubbing that cost them control of Congress. "Despite the absence of a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by an attack upon the United States," Massie said in a speech on the House floor, "Secretary Hegseth knowingly executed and implemented unlawful orders to initiate war against a foreign nation." Massie said Hegseth "has demonstrated that he will remain a threat to the Constitution if allowed to remain in office, and has acted in a manner grossly incompatible with his duties and the rule of law." His actions thus "warrant impeachment and trial, removal from office and disqualification to hold and enjoy any office of honor, trust or profit under the United States," the Kentucky Republican said. President Trump on Monday pledged to support Hegseth while he faces impeachment. "Yeah, I'll stand by him," he told CNN , adding that he believes Massie "has a lot of hatred in his heart." Hegseth leaves a meeting of defense ministers in the Philippines on Oct. 28. Pool via Getty Images Massie — who in May lost his bid for reelection to Ed Gallrein, a Trump-backed challenger, in the GOP primary — first introduced articles of impeachment against Hegseth in September. But House Speaker Mike Johnson later canceled the final scheduled voting day before the midterm recess, delaying a vote. It's unclear whether an impeachment effort will succeed in the House, which is still under Republican control, but Massie told ABC News that he's "confident there will be enough GOP defectors for it to pass." To do so, the resolution requires a simple majority, meaning that just three Republicans would need to vote with all Democrats to prevail. A vote could come as soon as this week. Trump has repeatedly insisted that he is not considering replacing his Pentagon chief, at least not yet. "No, I think he's doing a very good job," Trump told reporters last week. The president also said he was unaware of a report that Hegseth has been quietly angling to fill the U.S. Senate seat that will be vacated by Tennessee GOP Sen. Marsha Blackburn, who was elected as the state's next governor. "I think he's doing a very good job, and I actually think he'd be very popular if he did that. But I haven't heard that at all," Trump said when asked if he would want the defense secretary to fill Blackburn's seat. CBS News , however, reported last week that Trump "has been asking advisers" whether he should stay or go. Hegseth, a former Fox News host who has served as defense secretary since January 2025, has been Trump's most visible cheerleader for the Iran war, which the U.S. and Israel initiated in February and which has led to surging oil prices. He has also been among the advisers urging Trump to restart the war. He and Adm. Brad Cooper, the head of U.S. Central Command, have supported a return to major combat operations against Iran during recent briefings on military options, the Wall Street Journal reported on Nov. 6, while Vice President JD Vance and special envoy Steve Witkoff have pushed for diplomacy to end the conflict. The U.S. Capitol building is seen in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 4. Kevin Carter/Getty Images Trump acknowledged on Nov. 4 that the Iran war had partly contributed to the midterm election rout that handed Democrats control of Congress. Vance was unequivocal. "The real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone," Vance wrote in a lengthy post on X . "The reason we lost is the war." The vice president did not call out Hegseth by name. But other Republicans did. Sen. Thom Tillis, a Republican from North Carolina, told CBS News that Hegseth faces "a reckoning." "He is one of the reasons why we don't have the funding or guarantee for defense that we need," Tillis said on election night. "I think after the election, we need to determine whether or not he's the best person to bring those needs to Congress." Tillis, who voted to confirm Hegseth last year, recently called on Trump to fire him. "I have never witnessed more inept management of the brave men and women who serve our country," Tillis wrote in a scathing assessment of Hegseth on X in September. "He is intimidated by competence and retreats to ginning up culture wars instead of soberly attending to the vital work of our national defense and the health and well-being of our fighting force. I urge the President to find a new leader at the Pentagon who will retain and empower our military talent rather than diminish it." Rep. James Comer of Kentucky, the Republican chairman of the House Oversight Committee, said on Nov. 6 that "there's a lot of questions about Hegseth." "We have no idea what the strategy is moving forward in Iran," Comer told NewsNation . "No one's happy about Iran." A fire burns at an oil depot in Tehran, Iran, on March 8 after U.S. and Israeli attacks. Hassan Ghaedi/Anadolu via Getty Images When Democrats take control of both the House and Senate next year, they will have the ability to call for hearings and launch investigations into virtually any aspect of the Trump administration — and Hegseth's handling of the military is high on their list. "In the majority, one of the first things we're gonna do is run Pete Hegseth out of town," Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York, the minority leader who is poised to become House speaker in January, said at a rally last month . Hegseth, for his part, has remained defiant. In a 5-and-a-half-minute video posted to X on Nov. 5, Hegseth defended the Iran war, touted changes he's implemented as Pentagon chief ("We ended the weird and the woke") and praised Trump's leadership while dismissing Massie's impeachment pursuit. "A disgruntled, defeated congressman along with all his Democrat allies has dropped sham impeachment articles against yours truly," Hegseth said. "It didn't work with President Trump and it won't work with me." Hegseth said on Monday that he's "not worried about" the impeachment efforts. The defense secretary said he would address the topic at a press conference at the Pentagon on Tuesday. articles.title: Mississippi Democrat calls out election forecasters for writing off his campaign
articles.summary: Mississippi Senate candidate Scott Colom (D) blasted prominent election forecasters for underestimating his chances of defeating Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R) in their election ratings, arguing that the grim predictions made it harder for Democrats to raise money and compete in the South. Colom, a Black attorney, has maintained a narrow lead over Hyde-Smith by less than 3,000 votes in one of the biggest surprises of last week’s midterm elections, with the race still too close to call. In a post on social media, Colom accused the nonpartisan election handicapper Cook Political Report and other unnamed election forecasters of relying on outdated assumptions about Southern elections and overlooking candidates who could make races in deep-red states competitive. “At some point, we have to talk about @CookPolitical and other ‘prognosticators’ who had me and other southern candidates labeled as solid R for much of the campaign cycle,” Colom wrote on the social platform X on Monday. “They made it much more difficult to fundraise and are part of the reason the South has been neglected for so long.” The Cook Political Report had initially rated the Mississippi Senate race as “Solid Republican,” citing doubts over the ability for a Democrat to challenge Hyde-Smith in a state President Trump carried by 24 percentage points in 2024. It later shifted to “Likely Republican” in October. Even as the race attracted more attention in the finals weeks before Election Day, forecasters remained skeptical of Colom’s chances in a state that hasn’t elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1982. An Oct. 30 analysis from Cook Political Report described Colom’s campaign as “admirable” but noted that Republicans believed a late influx of campaign spending had helped shore up Hyde-Smith’s reelection bid. Colom’s campaign raised $4.4 million compared to Hyde-Smith’s $6.3 million, though both parties have recently ramped up the pressure to raise more money in the surprisingly tight Senate race. Colom said the forecasters avoid accountability when wrong about their predictions, and accused an unnamed Cook Political Report analyst of dismissing his attempts to explain why their assessment of his campaign was incorrect. “One of their ‘analysts’ was extremely condescending to me (not Jessica) when I tried to make my pitch for why they were wrong about my rating like he knew something about MS politics when he’s never been to the Sip,” he wrote, clarifying that Senate and Governors editor Jessica Taylor was not the individual to whom he was referring. He added that the attitude had hurt other Southern candidates in the midterms, including Louisiana Senate candidate Jamie Davis, who narrowly lost to Rep. Julia Letlow (R-La.). articles.title: Supreme Court allows Big Bend border wall plans in win for Trump
articles.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday cleared the way for the Trump administration to bypass regulations and build a border barrier in Texas's scenic Big Bend National park — a project that has been paused several times in recent months amid lawsuits and opposition on both the left and the right. In an unsigned opinion, the court said that Congress had expressed a "clear preference for expeditious border construction," which outweighs "any aesthetic, recreational, and environmental harm." Previously, a federal judge had halted the project , allowing litigation to proceed without further loss of protected wilderness and questioning whether Big Bend National Park meets Congress's fast-track definition of an area with "high illegal entry." The Supreme Court effectively dismissed those arguments. In August, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) Commissioner Rodney Scott announced that he was temporarily "pausing all construction activity" in Big Bend. "Last night I put a pause on all activity in that park as far as construction goes until I can get down there and do a personal evaluation," Scott said in a video posted to social media , adding that he would "talk to some stakeholders, talk to some local law enforcement in that area" to "ensure that we secure our borders while simultaneously protecting BBNP for generations to come." CBP is pausing all construction activity in Big Bend National Park while I visit and conduct a personal, on-the-ground evaluation. CBP is firmly committed to protecting America,  and that includes our national treasures like Big Bend National Park (BBNP). We know the current and… pic.twitter.com/UkmzvTluwH — CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott (@CBPCommissioner) August 17, 2026 Earlier that month, government contractors started bulldozing sensitive areas of Big Bend as part of the Trump administration's $46.5 billion push to expand border barriers along the U.S.-Mexico border — a move that triggered fierce bipartisan backlash. "I believe in border security 100%," Terrell County Sheriff Thaddeus Cleveland, a Republican and former Border Patrol agent, told Fox San Antonio . "Believe in even installation of barriers where they're needed. But I can tell you that specific area ... even just what they've done, unnecessary." Republican Sen. John Cornyn of Texas also sent a letter to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin relaying his constituents' concerns. "My constituents believe that the 1,000-foot riverbank cliffs and remote Big Bend terrain offers its own source of deterrence for any illegal migrants crossing into the United States," Cornyn wrote. "Many residents that live and work around the parks are also concerned that a physical wall, which would be accompanied by lighting systems, access roads, and maintenance corridors, would (1) ruin the beauty, landscape, and wildlife of the park, (2) threaten culturally significant Native American sites, (3) disrupt wildlife migration, (4) limit access to the Rio Grande River, and (5) significantly harm the local economy as tourism is a major economic driver for the region." Since returning to office in January 2025, President Trump has taken action to remove protections from more than 86 million acres of public lands, according to a recent analysis by the Center for American Progress (CAP), a liberal think tank. Here's everything you need to know about what's happening in Big Bend — and how it connects to Trump's broader agenda. What is Big Bend National Park? Established in 1944, Big Bend encompasses more than 800,000 acres of scorching Chihuahuan desert, cool, craggy peaks and fertile Rio Grande valley. It's located in a remote pocket of the Lone Star State formed by a huge southward dip in the river, and it contains within its boundaries 517 miles of U.S.-Mexico border. The park's diverse landscape is home to 56 species of reptiles, 75 species of mammals, more than 450 species of birds and more than 1,200 species of plants. Sea fossils, dinosaur bones and volcanic dikes have also been found there. Big Bend National Park is located along the U.S.-Mexico border, with the Rio Grande serving as the boundary. Getty Images The National Park Service describes Big Bend as a "hiker's paradise," with more than 150 miles of desert and mountain trails — including the 1,500-foot vertical limestone walls of Santa Elena Canyon and Lost Mine's sweeping valley views. Designated a Gold Tier International Dark Sky Park in 2012, Big Bend is one of the best places in the U.S. to see the Milky Way at night. "Easily top 10 park for me," one Reddit commenter wrote . "Borderline top 5." "It's so far out there  — really remote — which helps make it feel more magical," another added. Is Trump really building a border wall in Big Bend? Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill — which passed in July 2025 over unanimous Democratic opposition — included $46.5 billion in funding for hundreds of miles of new border barriers, and early CBP maps showed "a bold line of wall structure along the floodplain of most of the Rio Grande in the high desert region of Far West Texas," according to the Washington Post . But after residents and local officials objected, the administration quietly altered its plans, nixing its usual 30-foot steel bollard fence in favor of 17 miles of "vehicle barriers" — interconnected steel X's, 4 to 6 feet in height — along with surveillance cameras, lights, sensors and a new patrol road that will run the length of the park, at a cost of $1.7 billion. In August, bulldozers belonging to Southwest Valley Constructors started work on the patrol road. According to the Post , " images show vehicle treads left behind on the dusty terrain as animals such as hoofed javelinas wander past. Construction crews were spotted surveying the land and marking the road's planned route." "Early construction activities such as clearing and grubbing have begun," a CBP spokesman confirmed in a statement to the outlet. Border barrier construction work near Santa Elena Canyon on Aug. 6. Natalie Newman/Center for Biological Diversity At the time, CBP denied that its contractors would have to dynamite the mountainside to complete the road — but advocates insisted that "if they're going to build on that [rock], there is no alternative to blasting," as Bob Krumenaker, former Big Bend superintendent for the National Park Service, told the Post. Krumenaker predicted that blasting would alter the view, disturb nesting falcons and send debris spilling into the Rio Grande. In August, the Daily Mail reported that "demolition crews have already begun blowing craters into the bedrock" with "sticks of TNT" just outside the park. "'They've been blowing things up for about the last two weeks," one border agent told the paper. "Underneath the surface is rock, not dirt. They have to blow it up in order to build the wall. No one knows about it because there's no one out here to see it, but the project is moving ahead." In response, a CBP spokesman told the Daily Mail that "construction crews are onsite re-grading roads that were damaged by recent storms that are required for access to conduct surveys." Wait, how can the administration build anything in a national park? In order to speed construction of the border wall — which slowed to a crawl during Trump's first term amid lawsuits and property ownership disputes — the Department of Homeland Security has waived its contractors from complying with dozens of laws, including the Endangered Species Act and the National Environmental Policy Act. This means CBP can disregard the project's impact on certain plants and animals while skipping lengthy reviews and avoiding public input. According to the Center for Biological Diversity , "the move marks the first time in American history that the federal government has cast aside a broad slate of environmental laws … in a national park." In his letter, Cornyn complained about the administration's lack of "coordination and communication" with "Texas stakeholders," saying it "has not been as fulsome as in prior years." "On April 16, fourteen Texas-Mexico Border County Judges wrote to you asking for DHS to engage with the communities they serve and have open communication about the upcoming installation of border security measures," Cornyn wrote. "To my knowledge, the county judges have not received a response to their April 16 letter." A bulldozer clears a path in Big Bend National Park on Aug. 6. Natalie Newman/Center for Biological Diversity The administration's approach to Big Bend is part of a larger pattern. In March 2025, Trump signed an executive order designed to expand logging and reduce oversight across about 250 million acres of national forests and protected public lands — a move that could damage fragile ecosystems, threaten old-growth forests, increase pollution and even worsen wildfires, according to environmentalists. In April, a border wall contractor partially bulldozed — or "inadvertently disturbed," as CBP later put it — a giant, ancient Native American etching in the floor of the Arizona desert. In July, the president signed proclamations to shrink two major national monuments in southern Utah — Bears Ears National Monument and Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument — by roughly 91% in order to open previously protected land to uranium and coal mining. Similar rollbacks have also occurred in Alaska, where the administration has opened new sites to oil drilling. All told, the Trump administration has "cumulatively removed or initiated removal of protections for more than 100 million acres of public lands across both terms," according to CAP — more than one-third of the amount of land that President Theodore Roosevelt initially protected during his time in office. How have people reacted? According to the Post, Big Bend "community members have sued the federal government in court, filed complaints with environmental protection agencies, opposed permits for contractors seeking use of local roads and wells, and demanded accountability in public meetings." Protesters gathered at the park in August to voice their opposition , and public officials from both parties have called the administration's project disruptive and redundant, noting that " near zero " crossings occur within the park itself. "God already built a wall through Big Bend — it's called the Chisos Mountains," then-Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico wrote on X . "We don't need to give billions of our tax dollars to out of state vendors. We don't need to desecrate this sacred land. We don't need this useless, disgraceful, corrupt Big Bend border wall." "The potential destruction from road construction over the rugged terrain of Mariscal Mountain is extreme," Texas Rep. Lloyd Doggett, also a Democrat, said in a July 31 news release . "Tons of rock blasted away could end up impacting Mariscal Canyon, the Rio Grande, and Mexico.  An incredible waste of both taxpayer money and an invaluable place of spectacular beauty!" "Major permanent infrastructure, accompanied by lighting systems, access roads, and maintenance corridors would permanently alter one of the most remote and ecologically significant border landscapes in the United States," five border sheriffs, including Cleveland, wrote in a March statement . "Border security is not a one-size-fits-all proposition. Strategies that may be appropriate in high-traffic urban sectors are not necessarily appropriate in geographically remote regions such as ours." "We are killing a gnat with a sledgehammer and wasting a colossal amount of money," Brewster County, Texas, Judge Greg Henington said at the time . Henington is a Republican. In August, U.S. House candidate Brandon Herrera — a Republican running to represent the Big Bend area in Congress — said in a statement that he opposes "any construction in the Big Bend area that disturbs the natural landscape and threatens the jobs that tourism brings where non-intrusive technology would do the job." GOP House Speaker Mike Johnson acknowledged in July that the administration should "take into account the local community's concerns." But he also argued that Trump's "border wall" won't always look like a literal wall. "When we say build a wall, in some respects, it's a metaphor," Johnson told reporters. "It means we have to have a border that is secure." articles.title: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
articles.summary: Fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France were affected last month [Getty Images] France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers across the country last month. Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression", adding those who were responsible would be hit with sanctions. Iran has yet to respond officially, but some Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless. The French hacking, which led to the destruction of tons of frozen and chilled food in France was followed by a similar attack against supermarkets across several other European countries. It is not known if the instances are linked. Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people". He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act". France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added. The Paris prosecutor said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with the IRGC as well as his two deputies. Laure Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC. Shahid Kaveh is the name given to a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian regime. In recent weeks, a number of commentators and politicians in Iran have argued that the country should extend any retaliation beyond the Middle East if the US and Israel resume the war they started earlier this year. If the IRGC carried out the cyber-attacks, it remains unclear whether they were part of Iran's deterrence strategy. On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France's supermarkets. More than 100 of Coopérative U's supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight. Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss. The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely. Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe. Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in countries including Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland. Separately in August a small number of US military bases had fridges mysteriously malfunction, spoiling food. This incident is also being investigated as deliberate cyber-attacks, Reuters news agency has reported, citing sources familiar with the matter. Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects. In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them. The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber-attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations. Additional reporting by Farshad Bayan, BBC Persian. articles.title: Trump's MAHA coalition faces new tensions as former officials trade accusations
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — A public spat between former Trump administration officials over alleged corruption in public health policymaking is the latest front in Republicans' postelection recriminations, a battle that has exposed fault lines within the White House and could reshape political alliances involving the influential Make America Healthy Again movement. The blowup began when Calley Means , a former top adviser to Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and a chief advocate for the MAHA movement , appeared on Joe Rogan's podcast Friday and accused Susie Wiles, James Blair and others of catering to foreign and domestic lobbyists at the expense of Americans' health. Wiles, who was recently replaced as White House chief of staff, and Blair, a top political adviser, have denied the allegations. Means' remarks came days after voters cast ballots in midterm elections where government corruption was among the top issues for voters who ousted Republicans and handed Democrats control of Congress. The issue overlaps with concerns from MAHA activists, who have been focused on combating what they see as systemic and harmful corporate influence over policymaking. MAHA became an important part of Trump's coalition after Kennedy endorsed him during the last presidential campaign, and fractures could create political headaches or new avenues for congressional investigations in the coming years. Zen Honeycutt, a former Kennedy campaign staffer and founder of the group Moms Across America, said Means is "amplifying the frustrations that a lot of MAHA folks have had the past few months and validating them." She's "excited for a new beginning" now that Trump has replaced Wiles with Stephen Miller, whom she views as more aligned with the movement. But Honeycutt hasn't ruled out working with Democrats, such as New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, whom she met with in July to discuss shared environmental priorities, including the pesticide glyphosate and artificial intelligence data centers. "The MAHA movement does not belong to any party or politician," Honeycutt said. Means alleges outside interests influenced policymaking On Rogan's show, Means recounted a conversation he had with Wiles about her declining to support certain MAHA initiatives because she needed donations from the sugar industry. "Calley, we can't do this. I need sugar money," he recalled Wiles saying to him. "I need the money from the sugar people to win the midterms." "There is a very concentrated group in the Trump administration that are antagonistic to what people voted for," Means said. Rogan's show was released Friday, shortly before Trump announced Wiles would step down as White House chief of staff. Means was hired as a White House adviser early in the second Trump administration. He used his perch at the Health and Human Services Department to attack the nation's leading physician groups, federal agencies and government scientists , claiming they only protect their own interests . Means left the Trump administration in October, without stating a reason for his exit. "She has taken a stranglehold on any policy decision" impacting the MAHA movement, alongside her former lobbying firm Ballard Partners, Means said about Wiles. Referring to Blair in the Rogan interview, Means said he has "explicitly catered to special interests against the will of the voters." He said he believed much of what he was alleging "happened without Trump's full knowledge." Blair, who previously served as a White House deputy chief of staff before taking an outside role in Trump's political operation, responded on social media that he was contemplating suing Means over his statements. In text messages between Means and Blair, viewed by The Associated Press, Blair told Means "if you get near slandering or defaming me I will sue you," and "if you are gonna try to knife me, I'm happy to return the favor." The White House denied Means' accusations. "The Trump Administration has never allowed and will never allow outside groups to influence policy decisions," White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster said. Brian Ballard, founder of Ballard Partners, denied communicating with top White House officials on glyphosate and other issues in a statement posted on social media. MAHA support may be up for grabs The extraordinary public fight, which was continuing on social media Monday, comes after MAHA had grown disenchanted over some of the administration's moves. In recent months, many grassroots MAHA activists who had initially hoped to collaborate with Trump's Environmental Protection Agency had soured on the agency and the administration, viewing them as infiltrated by lobbyist interests. They pointed to various insiders in the agricultural and chemical industries who'd secured high-level positions in the EPA and blamed them for the administration's failure to pass meaningful reforms to address microplastics in drinking water or pesticides on farms. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin promised last December to unveil a formal agenda of MAHA policies he would act on. But by the summer, the so-called MAHA agenda had never surfaced, and an EPA spokesperson told the AP that MAHA is an ongoing effort, rather than a single report. That apparent reversal prompted several activists to say they planned to vote on issues over party in November's elections. "People are done with the profits of corporations being prioritized over public health," Alexandra Muñoz, a molecular toxicologist who collaborates with MAHA activists on certain issues, told the AP in July. "And I think that will have an important role in the midterms." The simmering MAHA frustration, coupled with Means' allegations, could put MAHA support in play for Democrats, something Means himself suggested over the weekend. "There's a lot of complicated issues that I'm sure Democrats are going to want to address. But when it comes to these issues on MAHA, I think there is huge opportunity in the next year to get some big things done," he told CBS' "Face the Nation." But doing so poses its own complications. Democrats who will take over both chambers of Congress next year could use Means' statements as a vehicle to begin investigations into White House officials. Some Democrats have long sought to investigate Kennedy over his upending of vaccine policy and his vast cuts to science research, among other decisions. Pushing hard against Kennedy, however, could complicate efforts to build closer ties with MAHA supporters, many of whom still view the health secretary positively. Means' interviews included a profuse defense of Kennedy, who some have speculated could attempt another run for president in 2028. Means called Kennedy a "hero" on the podcast interview. articles.title: Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assaults
articles.summary: Russell Brand, the British former comedian and actor, has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for raping a woman and sexually assaulting three more. Handing down the sentence Monday at Southwark Crown Court in London, Judge Joel Bennathan said Brand told a series of lies throughout the trial, adding he had displayed a "casual and arrogant disregard" for women who said 'No' to him. "About 20 years ago, Russell Brand, you were becoming famous," Bennathan said. "You were clever — and in many people's eyes, funny and charismatic. You had also become a sexual predator." He added, "Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever they drink, they retain the right to say 'no' and to demand justice from criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Russell Brand, act without their consent." Brand was supported in court by his wife, Laura Gallacher, and his father, Ron. He is expected to serve at least two-thirds of that sentence — around seven years — before being eligible for release. Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault on Nov. 5. He was acquitted of two rape counts and one count of attempted indecent assault. Prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones called Brand a ruthless, calculating and manipulative "sexual predator" who treated women as a "disposable commodity." "Mr. Brand abused the influence and power that came with his fame," Karmy-Jones said. "He used it to facilitate an access to women without which the offending could not have taken place. It also fed his own view that he could commit such offenses with impunity." Ahead of his sentencing, one woman, who was sexually assaulted by Brand in 2004 or 2005, told the court on Monday in her impact statement : "Russell Brand is a sexual predator who has no remorse.” Another woman, who was raped by the comedian in 2009 after meeting him at a comedy show in London, said she was "living with trauma." She said his fame made it "difficult to escape reminders of what had happened," BBC reported . She said she was worried after the attack that she might have HIV, struggled to eat and sleep, took nearly three months off work and abandoned the career she had embarked upon. "Although the rape was 17 years ago, she still finds it affects her ability to form new friendships and to know when she can trust people," the judge said. A third woman who was assaulted by Brand while working on a Channel 4 documentary said that, following the attack, she felt like she had "lost my trust in people." Reflecting on the incident, she added: "I felt powerless in that moment." Last week, Megyn Kelly, the former Fox News host, reacted to Brand's conviction in disbelief. "I don't believe the charges, and I don't have to believe them just because a jury came through with the opposite conclusion," she said in a YouTube livestream . The next day, in a comment on X, Elon Musk described Brand's conviction for offenses nearly 20 years old as a " crazy legal standard ." England doesn't have a statute of limitations for rape or sexual assault. Brand became a household name in the U.K. in the 2000s as a comedian and broadcaster and had well-documented issues with drugs and alcohol. He went on to star in the movies Get Him to the Greek in 2010 and Arthur the following year. He married singer Katy Perry in October 2010, but Brand filed for divorce in December 2011, citing irreconcilable differences. Their divorce was finalized in July 2012. The claims against Brand were made by six different women, spanning from 1999 to 2009. None of the women knew each other, but came forward to police following a TV documentary and press reports in 2023, in which anonymous allegations were made by other women. Laura Brand, the wife of British actor and comedian Russell Brand, arrives at Southwark Crown Court on Nov. 9. REUTERS / REUTERS During the trial, the court heard tearful testimony from the six accusers, who are all entitled to lifelong anonymity. According to the Associated Press, the convictions included a rape that took place in 2009, involving a woman who went to Brand's home after meeting him at one of his shows. She said she had engaged in consensual sex, but that Brand then raped her and removed a condom in the process. Brand was also convicted of sexually assaulting a woman when he grabbed her breasts at a London bar in 2004. He was also found guilty over an incident in 2009, in which he demanded a woman give him a massage in front of two of his colleagues and then put his head in her groin. A third complaint of sexual assault ended in a guilty verdict when Brand was found guilty of pushing a woman who worked at a radio station up against a wall and forcibly kissing her. Brand denied the charges and said he had never forced anyone to do something against their will. Footage released by London's Metropolitan Police Service after the verdict shows Brand being interviewed by police in December 2023. "As I've repeatedly stated publicly and written about extensively, I led a very promiscuous life in the past, which I've spent years openly denouncing," Brand can be seen saying. "I've never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity." He said he did "not recall the names" of the complainants, or meeting them, adding, "However, it's entirely possible that I may have encountered them and we may have engaged in consensual sexual activity or physical contact that's been since reimagined." Following the verdict, the Metropolitan Police Service told Yahoo that Brand, 51, was facing further allegations of rape from two women. "The suspect has previously been interviewed under caution in connection with the allegations," the force said. Brand has not been charged in relation to these claims. The head of the Met Police, Mark Rowley, has urged any other victims of Brand to contact the police. "There's two more rape allegations that we're looking at. We're encouraging anybody else to come forward if there's any other allegations," he told reporters on Nov. 6. He later said that he "wouldn't be surprised if many, many more come forward. … This shows that powerful people can be brought down so you are safe stepping forward and we will support and try and bring that person to justice." articles.title: Ohio State suspends fraternity after video shows 2 men engulfed in flames
articles.summary: COLUMBUS, Ohio (AP) — A fraternity at Ohio State University has been temporarily suspended while authorities investigate a video that appears to show two panicked men engulfed in flames. A video shared on social media shows a large group of people standing outside, many wearing the school's red and white colors, laughing and shouting while a man sits on the ground with his sweatpants on fire. He then lunges at a second person and tackles him. The second man's clothing also catches fire, and they both roll on the ground removing their clothes as several onlookers intervene. One appears to be holding a small fire extinguisher. University spokesperson Benjamin Johnson said the school has placed Sigma Alpha Epsilon fraternity on interim suspension while it investigates, and has referred the matter to university and Columbus police. The university did not say how the fraternity is linked to the event, whether the burned men are students or what condition they were in Monday. "The university is aware of this extremely concerning incident, and the individuals in question are receiving medical care," Johnson said in a statement. "Ohio State is committed to a safe and healthy environment and expects students and student organizations to uphold that commitment and the university's values." Columbus Police Sgt. Joe Albert said it appears the matter took place on Saturday. Police did not receive any calls for service at the location, but someone called police Sunday evening reporting that the video was circulating online, he said. Steve Mitchell, CEO of Sigma Alpha Epsilon, said behavior that violates its high standards has no place in its organization and it will take appropriate action to hold those responsible accountable based on the investigation. "We take this matter seriously and are actively investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident while working closely with university officials and local law enforcement," he said in a statement. More than 60,000 students are enrolled at the university. The episode comes as fraternities are back in the national spotlight in the wake of a former Cornell University student's lawsuit saying she was gang raped at a fraternity party in 2024. ___ Ramer reported from Concord, New Hampshire. articles.summary: 摩根士丹利分析师Shawn Kim再度向内存行业发出警告，这一次他瞄准的是行业“2028年的盈利悬崖”。 据追风交易台消息，在11月9日发布的最新研报中，Shawn Kim全面下调三星电子和SK海力士目标价，并将三星电子升为新首选股，取代SK海力士。他在报告中写道： “对内存的担忧，与其说是美国中期选举后数据中心建设延迟或AI需求的问题，不如说是'2028盈利悬崖'叙事的风险——市场对内存增长动能的可持续性持怀疑态度，因为供给正开始追上需求。” 他认为，市场争论焦点已从近期基本面转向“2028盈利悬崖”—— 2027年底新产能陆续投产、数据中心建设延迟、HBM溢价收窄等多重压力叠加，内存超级周期的可持续性存疑。 Shawn Kim据此将SK海力士和三星的长期利润率假设向历史均值大幅压缩，直接拉低了两家公司的估值模型输出值。 这并非Shawn Kim第一次在内存行业高景气阶段发出警告。 华尔街见闻提及 ，他曾于2021年8月发布《存储，凛冬将至》，精准踩中此后长达两年的半导体下行周期；2024年9月，其关于HBM供过于求可能性的报告，被视为当年三星和SK海力士股价急跌的导火索之一；今年 7月21日他再度发布报告 警告称，AI驱动的半导体存储行业狂欢正接近拐点，内存合同价格预计将于第四季度见顶，而后SK海力士与三星电子股价再出现了一次急跌。 这些事迹也令他在韩国市场赢得 “韩国半导体死神” 的绰号。此次报告，是他在内存AI交易持续去泡沫化背景下的又一次警示。 估值重置：目标价大幅下调，三星升为首选 Shawn Kim此次调整幅度显著。 SK海力士目标价从260万韩元下调38%至160万韩元 ，对应2027年预期市净率约1.8倍，较当前参考价113.2万韩元仍有约41%上行空间，维持增持评级。 三星电子普通股目标价从38.1万韩元下调19%至30.9万韩元 ，优先股目标价从30.48万韩元下调至24.72万韩元，两者均维持增持，且三星电子普通股被升为新首选股。 目标价下调的核心驱动，是 Shawn Kim对两家公司长期可持续利润率假设的大幅下修。 Shawn Kim此前假设2035年前DRAM长期可持续利润率约为60%，此次将SK海力士2029-2035年DRAM运营利润率均值下调至约32%（接近2010-2025年历史均值31%），三星则下调至约39%。与此同时，HBM相对于普通DRAM的溢价，被假设从2029年的20个百分点逐步收窄至2033年归零。 报告同时上调了两家公司2026-2028年的近期盈利预测，主要受益于回购计划带来的股份数量减少。 SK海力士2026-2028年每股收益预测分别变动-1%、+22%、+29%；三星2026-2028年每股收益预测分别上调3%、16%、26%。 “2028盈利悬崖”：四大压力叠加 Shawn Kim在报告中明确指出，“2028盈利悬崖”是当前内存投资最核心的争论。他列出了四个令长期利润率假设承压的关键因素。 第一，供给响应快于预期。 2027年底前后将有新产能陆续投产，近期更高的第四季度出货量指引和更快的制程迁移，意味着比此前预期更多的比特供给。中国供应商进入消费市场，也将对大宗内存定价形成额外压力。 第二，2028年数据中心建设延迟。 大摩全球主题研究团队将约5GW的美国数据中心项目从2028年推迟至2029年。据此，全球数据中心新增容量2028年同比增速从约21%下调至9%，2029年则反弹至20%。这可能削弱内存的供给紧张程度和定价能力。 第三，BOM成本约束限制内容增长。 内存已占AI服务器物料清单（BOM）成本约60%，这正迫使买家将高密度96GB/128GB配置降规格至64GB RDIMM。NAND现货价格在过去两周内下跌约20%，512Gb TLC晶圆价格跌至约15美元，较3月高点下跌27-29%，并低于7-8月低点，为合同市场带来额外定价风险。 第四，HBM溢价正在收窄。 大摩将SK海力士的HBM运营利润率预测从78-80%下调至约70%，三星从约80%下调至65-72%。随着竞争加剧和普通DRAM价格正常化，HBM持续维持高溢价的可能性下降。 周期定位：估值已调整，但盈利切割尚未到来 尽管发出警告，Shawn Kim并未全面看空。他在报告中对当前市场位置做出了较为细致的判断。 报告指出，自6月高点以来，费城半导体指数（SOX）12个月远期市盈率已从26.3倍腰斩至13.4倍，是互联网泡沫破裂以来最大幅度的估值压缩之一，而同期市场一致预期每股收益反而上升了24%。目前约13倍的远期市盈率，已与过去历次下行周期的中位数低谷估值（13.4倍）基本持平，处于2022年10月美联储加息低谷以来的最低水平。 估值已经完成了它该做的事。现在的变量是盈利线。Kim回顾了2000年以来11次SOX下行周期，发现其中9次主要由估值压缩驱动，而非盈利下调。只有在2000-2002年和2007-2008年两次需求真正崩塌时，盈利才出现超过50%的深度下修。 第二波下跌需要2028年盈利预测像2000-2002年和2007-2008年那样腰斩——这不是我们的基准情景，但这正是为什么盈利削减阶段，而非估值，才是现在最需要关注的事情。 Kim同时指出，AI供应链EPS修正广度自2026年7月峰值以来持续收窄——内存板块3个月均值从69%降至53%，AI计算从55%降至45%，网络从54%降至40%——但仍为正值，即盈利预测仍在上调，只是速度放缓。 三星vs海力士：周期末段，质量为王 在个股选择上，Kim将三星电子升为首选，逻辑在于周期末段更偏好“最大、资本最充裕、规模最强的科技龙头”。 报告认为，三星的HBM市场份额有望在2027年实现反超——据TrendForce预测，三星2027年HBM出货量将增长约82%至210亿Gb（市占率约39%），超越SK海力士的200亿Gb（约37%）。与此同时，三星更多元化的业务结构（包括非内存业务的潜在复苏）提供了额外支撑。在当前参考价18.87万韩元下，大摩30.9万韩元的目标价隐含约64%的上行空间。 SK海力士则维持增持，Kim认为其HBM领导地位、强劲的2027年盈利以及长期协议（LTA）对2028年的保护，仍构成支撑。但报告明确表示，目标价下调“反映了2028年后超额盈利期缩短”。 报告对最坏情景也有所描述：若AI融资成本上升或AI变现进展不及预期，买家可能暂停采购，已承诺的产能将面临需求不足的风险。 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ 以上精彩内容来自 追风交易台 。 articles.title: 能控制机器人拧瓶盖、解魔方和画画！Fable 5.2的具身智能能力实现“惊人跃迁”
articles.summary: Anthropic最新旗舰模型Claude Fable 5.2在机器人控制领域交出了一份令业界侧目的成绩单——作为一款通用大模型，它在双臂仿真机器人基准测试中的得分较上一代翻了逾两倍，并在真机演示中完成了拧瓶盖、解魔方和画画等操作任务。 11月9日，Anthropic正式发布Claude Fable 5.2。在RoboDojo双臂仿真机器人基准测试中， Fable 5.2平均成功率达64.9%，上一代Fable 5.1仅为27.6%，一代更新提升了37.3个百分点，得分翻2.35倍。 同期对比中， Claude Opus 5.5得分39.4%，GPT-6 Astra得分29.8%，Fable 5.2均大幅领先。 Anthropic官方表示，该模型在机器人控制方面的表现“优于大多数专为机器人控制而设计的AI系统”。 这一进展对具身智能赛道的冲击不容忽视。 过去业界普遍认为，机器人需要专门训练具身模型和世界模型，以解决空间理解、动作规划和长程控制等问题。而此次Fable 5.2以通用大模型身份实现这一幅度的跃升，直接引发市场对专用具身AI公司竞争格局的重新审视。 在A股市场，Fable 5.2发布当日，宇树科技涨近8%，市值重回3000亿元上方，福莱新材、亿嘉和涨停，安培龙、汉威科技等具身智能相关标的整体走强。 通用模型打入具身智能腹地 Fable 5.2在机器人领域的突破，核心在于其泛化能力——即完成此前没有明确训练过的操作任务。 Anthropic官方表示：“Fable 5.2在控制物理机器人方面展现出大幅提升的能力， 甚至包括从未被明确训练过的任务。 ”在真机演示中，Fable 5.2控制机械臂完成了拧瓶盖、操作魔方和画画等任务。 值得关注的是， 就在Fable 5.2发布前后，前特斯拉Optimus机器人模型研究员Bingjie Tang宣布加入Anthropic。 她在X平台发文称：“很高兴分享，我已加入Anthropic！期待向这支出色的团队学习，并在AI前沿探索令人兴奋的问题。” 据悉， Bingjie Tang此前在Tesla Optimus负责机器人灵巧操作，涉及数据采集、策略训练、评估和真机部署 ，并曾在NVIDIA机器人实验室从事大量Sim-to-Real研究。 科技博主Max For AI在X上评论： “随着通用大模型的能力持续提升，前沿实验室正在越来越认真地探索物理世界，而那些真正做过机器人训练和部署的人，也开始进入大模型实验室。” 天风海外科技&传媒互联网研报指出，这一进展说明 “Anthropic战略正在锚定超长程任务，算力需求的增量或许更多来自过去做不完、现在能交给上千个Agent连跑几十小时的超长程任务”。 不过，Reddit机器人社区r/robotics中也有用户对此提出质疑。有网友援引斯坦福机器人学博士Aiden Swann的分析指出，GPT-6 Astra此前被发现在给定陌生机器人运动学参数时，输出结果与熟悉的Franka Panda机器人高度吻合，暗示存在记忆特定机器人知识而非真正泛化推理的可能。该网友表示，Fable 5.2是否存在类似情况同样难以独立核实。 专用具身模型，还有多少护城河？ 能力数字和人才流向叠加，让一些从业者开始重新审视具身智能公司的竞争格局。 此前，具身智能公司的竞争对手，通常被认为是其他机器人公司。而现在，Fable 5.2的这次更新让部分业内人士意识到，通用大模型正在成为一个新的变量。 不过，需要指出的是，RoboDojo目前是仿真环境下的评测，真实物理部署与仿真之间仍存在差距。Fable 5.2在真机演示中完成了拧瓶盖、解魔方和画画，但演示视频经过剪辑和加速处理——Reddit用户在帖子中提到，“机器人停顿的部分已被剪掉，视频也经过了大幅加速”。 具身智能公司的护城河是否真的在收窄，还需要更多真实场景的验证。 但有一点已经确定：通用大模型正在以更快的速度进入机器人控制这个过去被认为需要专用模型才能解决的领域。 单任务成本大幅压缩，Agent编排效率提升 机器人能力之外，Fable 5.2在成本结构上的变化同样值得关注。 据天风海外科技&传媒互联网研报， Fable 5.2在中档努力等级下的得分已超过Fable 5.1的最高分，单任务成本约为后者的三成。 Fable 5.1此前仅下调了缓存价格，而Fable 5.2则将标准输入、输出价格一并下调20%——新定价为每百万输入Token 8美元、每百万输出Token 40美元，较上一代的10美元和50美元均有所下降。 在官方Agent编程基准上，综合更少的token用量与更低的token单价，单任务成本约降七成。研报总结认为， “Fable用更少的输出token拿到了更高分，叠加单价下调，单任务成本快速降低”。 在长程协作能力方面，Anthropic展示了一项费马大定理形式化证明实验：两组各约1000个同型号Agent，运行30小时后，Fable 5.2将已有证明完整写成了机器可校验的代码，而Opus 5.5仅完成约27%，且延长运行时间后几乎毫无进展。在AA综合智能指数v5排名中，Fable 5.2位列第一，大幅超过Google Carbon。 IPO路演同步推进，估值承压 此次模型发布与Anthropic的IPO进程几乎同步。据天风海外科技&传媒互联网研报，Anthropic最早可能于香港时间11月10日19时（美股盘前）提交带发行价区间的招股书修订稿，路演预计于当晚21时启动。 据彭博报道，部分潜在买家给出的公司估值低至1.1万亿美元。《华尔街日报》此前报道称，公司目标于11月19日或20日挂牌上市，公司高管正与高盛和摩根士丹利的银行家密切沟通，商讨发行价格区间。 据路透报道，Anthropic拟通过发行新股在IPO中募集高达693亿美元资金，招股价区间为每股70美元至80美元。Anthropic拟在IPO中发行8.66666664亿股A类普通股。Anthropic表示，英伟达、AMD、博通、美光、微软及台积电七家科技巨头将以IPO发行价合计投入260亿美元进行私募配售。 在AI概念股经历剧烈波动的背景下，Anthropic选择在路演节点前发布Fable 5.2，意在向潜在投资者展示其在企业软件、科学研究和高价值专业工作流中的技术竞争力与商业化潜力。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 信心为0！高盛解读对冲基金仓位："投降式清仓"，疫情以来最大亏损
articles.summary: 上周，对冲基金终于“举手投降”。高盛最新数据显示，美国基本面多空基金单周大幅削减杠杆，去杠杆规模创2020年3月新冠疫情暴跌以来最大，净杠杆率跌至五年来0百分位，美国股票选手的仓位之轻，为过去五年所未见。与此同时，科技股遭遇的抛售规模已远超今年夏季那轮动荡，CTA量化策略仍在持续卖出，市场几乎所有情绪指标均在发出恐慌信号。 周一（11月9日），高盛大宗经纪数据显示， 美国基本面多空基金上周总杠杆率单周下降8.7个百分点，为2020年3月新冠疫情以来最大单周降幅，净杠杆率下降3.7个百分点至43.3%，处于五年回溯期的第0百分位。 高盛交易员Pierre Saboureault在周一的报告中总结称，去杠杆已加速至7月以来最高速度，基本面多空基金净杠杆率同时触及1年、3年和5年低点，上周四出现了“投降式”清仓的典型特征。 科技股首当其冲。 自10月初以来，高盛美国交易台客户已净卖出逾300亿美元科技股（TMT及通信服务），远超今年7月动量回调期间约210亿至230亿美元的抛售规模。与此同时，CTA量化策略上周五天内卖出约116亿美元标普期货和30亿美元纳指期货，且据模型预测， 未来一周仍将在各种情景下持续卖出 。 疫情以来最大去杠杆：净杠杆跌至五年零百分位 高盛交易员Nelson Armbrust在11月9日的“今日要点”报告中详细呈现了这场去杠杆的规模。 美国基本面多空基金总杠杆率下降8.7个百分点至207.5%（一年期第26百分位），净杠杆率下降3.7个百分点至43.3%（五年期第0百分位）。 经贝塔调整后的总杠杆率单周下跌近16个百分点，年初至今总杠杆率下降11个百分点，净杠杆率下降11.6个百分点，抹去了2025年全年21.9个百分点总杠杆率增幅的一半以上。多空比率1.527处于三年和五年期第1百分位。 Armbrust表示，“这是仓位正在清理的强烈信号。” 值得注意的是，若将宏观账户和系统化账户纳入全球大宗经纪账簿，整体总杠杆率实际上微升0.1个百分点至314.2%（过去一年第85百分位），但净杠杆率滑至第4百分位，多空比率降至第3百分位。 换言之，市场上仍有大量敞口，但几乎毫无信念。 从全球视角看，Saboureault的数据显示，全球股票遭净卖出（一年期-1.0个标准差），去杠杆步伐加快（一年期-0.8个标准差，为7月以来最大美元去杠杆规模）， 做多头寸的卖出规模是空头回补的5倍 。个股已连续第8周遭净卖出，宏观产品则连续第3周获净买入。全球基本面多空净杠杆率45.3%为过去12个月最低，处于1年和3年期第0百分位，多空比率为高盛账簿过去五年最低。 摩根士丹利此前曾指出，今夏及10月的持续去风险是L/S基金15年来最长的持续去风险阶段——而那还是上周"血洗"发生之前的判断。上周过后，美国净杠杆率从摩根士丹利所记录的51%进一步跌至高盛数据的43%。 科技股遭历史级抛售，工业股创五年最大净卖出 科技板块是此轮抛售的重灾区。 信息技术板块为全球及美国净卖出规模最大的板块，本周全球信息技术股的净卖出比例与高盛自2016年以来记录中最大净卖出周基本持平，且过去五个月内已有4次跻身历史前五大净卖出周。 高盛证券经纪人Robbie Stankard指出，以百分比计，本周全球科技股卖出规模与2024年10月中旬及9月的情况相当，均为高盛自2016年以来记录中最大净卖出周。 高盛交易员John Flood在其题为"翻篇上周"的报告中写道： 自10月初以来，高盛美国交易台客户已净卖出约300亿美元科技股（TMT及通信服务），其中上周贡献约60亿美元。 相比之下，7月动量回调期间的净卖出规模约为210亿至230亿美元，当前这轮抛售已超出30%至40%。唯一的积极信号是：11月6日（周五）是连续7个交易日中首次出现科技股净买入，规模约10亿美元。 工业板块同样未能幸免。 工业股为全球第二大净卖出板块，且创下五年来最大百分比净卖出，已连续第4周遭净卖出。 子板块层面，电气设备、建筑产品、航空航天与国防、贸易公司及分销商领跌，客运航空和机械获净买入。Stankard指出，电气设备和建筑产品领跌并非偶然——这正是数据中心电力相关交易。 从年初至今的累计情况看，TMT板块净卖出已回落至7月低点附近，工业板块上周五天内的卖出规模超过3个标准差，为美国各板块之最。 业绩方面， 高盛大宗经纪估算显示，美国基本面多空基金上周亏损1.94%，全球同类基金亏损1.48%，而标普500全收益指数同期下跌4.74%。美国股票选手年初至今回报率仅为5.47%，落后于标普500的8.43%。科技主题基金处境更为惨烈，至周四已抹去全年涨幅。 仓位结构：Mag 7仍近历史高位，住宅与电力转为净空 尽管经历了疫情以来最大规模的去杠杆，高盛账簿中仍有若干值得关注的仓位结构。Flood列出了当前大宗经纪账簿中五个突出的板块： Mag 7及超大规模云计算（净配置仍接近历史高位） 住宅/房屋建筑商（账簿净空，多空比率处于五年低位） 餐饮（多空比率处于五年低位） 电力/美国电气设备（账簿净空，多空比率处于五年低位） 中小市值生物科技（仍为净多，多空比率超过3，但处于约三年低位） 最引人注目的是：在经历疫情以来最大去杠杆之后，对Mag 7及超大规模云计算的净配置仍接近历史高位，而账簿已对住宅和电力/电气设备转为净空。 换言之，基金广泛抛售科技股的同时，仍死守"出钱方"（即超大规模云计算巨头）的多头仓位。若市场进一步恶化，这一最后的拥挤交易或将成为下一个被抛售的目标。 CTA量化策略：各种情景下均为卖家，最多或再抛450亿美元 上周，CTA量化策略充当了下行加速器。 据估算，CTA上周五天内卖出约116亿美元标普期货和30亿美元纳指期货。 更令人担忧的是后续压力。 Saboureault的系统化策略摘要显示，系统化/CTA信号目前在全球50%至60%的股票市场呈负值，涵盖标普500及多数主要市场。 Stankard的情景分析显示， 未来一周，无论市场走势如何，CTA均为卖家 ： 平盘情景 ：卖出约233亿美元（其中标普约311亿美元） 上涨情景 ：卖出约39亿美元（其中标普约231亿美元） 下跌情景 ：卖出约487亿美元（其中标普约315亿美元） 未来一个月，仅在强劲上涨情景下，CTA才转为买家（买入约740亿美元，其中标普约144亿美元）；下跌情景下，全球股票卖出规模可达约1495亿美元。 标普500的关键技术位：短期约7675点，中期约7549点，长期约7084点。目前指数收盘价均高于上述水平，这正是量化策略持续卖出的原因。 恐慌信号全面亮起，唯一例外是高盛自身情绪综合指标 多项市场情绪指标已发出强烈恐慌信号。 高盛“恐慌指数” ：Armbrust指出，该指数读数超过9历史上是较好的买入机会，上周四触及9.57，周末收于9.2。 “倍数惊喜比率” ：高盛衍生品专家与策略师Brian Garrett创建的这一指标衡量资产单日涨跌幅相对于前一日期权隐含波动率的倍数。 标普500本周该指标创19年来最大值，纳指排名第二，罗素2000排名前五——期权市场对此次波动的低估程度堪称二十余年来之最。 市场微观结构同样承压：标普期货盘口深度已跌至415万美元，远低于1140万美元的均值；1个月隐含相关性从夏季的不足10%跳升至约26%；纳指与标普隐含波动率之差扩大至近9个百分点，逼近夏季动量崩溃时创下的12.6点纪录；看跌期权偏斜维持在1.20的高位，看涨期权偏斜则跌至0.76。 高盛风险偏好指数（GSRAII） 已跌至-0.65，但尚未触及Armbrust所称的-1强买入信号水平。2020年3月新冠疫情低点时该指数为-2.03。 散户投资者也开始动摇。 Saboureault对散户的一词评价是“眨眼了”。上周出现了自6月初以来最负面的两个日度买卖偏斜读数，标普500散户净买入两度跌破零。AAII调查显示，截至11月4日当周，看空比例跳升7个百分点至48.4%，较历史均值高出17个百分点；CNN恐惧与贪婪指数从19小幅回升至24，但仍处于"极度恐惧"区间。 唯一的例外是高盛自身的美国股票情绪指标（Sentiment Indicator）。 该综合指标涵盖机构、散户和境外投资者共九项仓位指标，实际上从+0.2上升至+0.6。轻仓信号的阈值为低于-1.0，目前远未触及。原因在于，持续买入的共同基金和境外投资者将该综合指标维持在正值区间，令"所有人都已出局"的反向看多信号尚不完整。 谁在接盘？共同基金与企业回购逆势买入 对冲基金大规模清仓的另一面，是“慢钱”的逆势买入。 共同基金方面 ，据EPFR数据，截至11月4日当周，全球股票基金净流入约890亿美元（前一周为560亿美元），其中约370亿美元流入美国；过去四周累计净流入约2650亿美元，其中约1110亿美元流入美国。 科技基金再度录得最大净流入，尽管AI相关股票正经历剧烈波动。 跨境资金流入美国基金的规模持续攀升，自2022年以来累计已接近1万亿美元。 企业回购方面 ，目前约90%的标普500成分股已退出回购静默期，预计本周末将升至约93%。高盛回购交易台报告显示，上周活动大幅加速，受选举后动能和活跃财报季推动， 可自由裁量的公开市场订单占比从前一周的22%跳升至33%，执行量约为去年日均水平的1.6倍。 2026年迄今回购授权规模已达1.5万亿美元，超过2025年全年1.37万亿美元的纪录。 不过，供给压力同样不容忽视——上周北美IPO及增发规模达163亿美元，年初至今累计达5360亿美元，企业回购仍需持续消化这一供给压力。 多空博弈：仓位洗牌后，市场底部或仍需等待CTA卖完 Flood尽管经历了艰难一周，仍列出四点维持建设性看法的理由：标普500第三季度每股盈利同比增速追踪至35%；市场广度大幅改善；标普500市盈率约18倍，处于过去十年第31百分位，通信服务板块更处于自身十年历史第4百分位；企业正在积极逢低买入。 据Armbrust引述的高盛半导体分析师观点称，相关股票已明显进入超卖区域，风险回报对部分个股具有吸引力，并点名看好英伟达、博通、应用材料及Lam Research。 然而，多重压力仍悬而未决。 Saboureault总结道：“油价下跌、收益率下跌，波动率需要继续企稳，资金才能重新入场。” 在波动率企稳、周二CPI数据及英伟达11月17日财报落地之前，上周或许是对冲基金的“投降时刻”，但 市场真正的底部，可能还需要等待CTA完成剩余的卖出程序。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: AI风暴重头戏：股价接近腰斩，“AI云双雄”CoreWeave和Nebius财报要来了
articles.summary: 在AI基础设施投资热潮遭遇债务成本上升的双重压力下，两家新兴云计算公司CoreWeave和Nebius的股价在短短一个月内双双接近腰斩。 本周，两家公司将相继在11月10日、11月12日发布三季度财报。这一时间节点颇为微妙——市场正在等待一个答案：这场抛售，究竟是过度反应，还是合理定价？ 从基本面数据看，两家公司的营收增长轨迹依然强劲，分析师预期2027年CoreWeave营收将翻倍、Nebius营收将增长逾两倍。但问题的症结不在营收，而在于支撑这一增长所背负的巨额债务。 为何股价在一个月内近乎腰斩 据IG首席市场分析师Chris Beauchamp撰文指出，Meta的信用违约互换（CDS）利差在10月下旬创下历史新高——此前Meta再度上调资本支出预期，投资者随即转向抛售AI基础设施链条中杠杆最高的一端，即"新云"（neocloud）公司。这类公司的数据中心支出往往是其年营收的数倍。 CoreWeave首当其冲。该公司背负约500亿美元债务，10月中旬其2031年到期债券收益率一度逼近16%，CDS利差扩大至约1200个基点——这是信用市场通常留给偿债能力存疑借款人的水平。 Nebius的债务规模相对较小，且刚刚签署了一笔35亿美元的融资安排，但股价跌幅与CoreWeave几乎相当。这表明，投资者在这轮抛售中并未做太多区分。 CoreWeave和Nebius股价在过去一个月内分别暴跌44%和36%。 财报预期：营收增长仍强劲，但亏损持续 CoreWeave 方面，市场共识预期三季度营收为35.5亿美元，StarMine智能预估为35.4亿美元，两者基本持平，隐含超预期幅度仅约0.06%。相比之下，一季度超预期幅度为5.73%，二季度收窄至0.59%，显示分析师预测已逐步跟上其增长节奏。EBITDA预期为20.5亿美元，对应约58%的利润率，但公司预计仍将录得每股亏损1.16美元，四季度有望收窄至0.55美元。 Nebius 方面，营收预期为9.08亿美元，SmartEstimate略高至9.16亿美元，预计正向惊喜幅度约0.96%。一季度和二季度的超预期幅度分别为7.43%和1.67%，同样呈收窄趋势。EBITDA预期3.53亿美元，对应约39%的利润率，预计每股亏损0.69美元，四季度或扩大至0.95美元，之后逐步改善。 多头逻辑：跌幅是否已过度反映悲观预期 从纯数字角度看，两家公司的成长故事依然引人注目。 据IG援引共识数据，CoreWeave今年营收预计为128.6亿美元，2027年有望升至264.7亿美元，增幅约106%；Nebius今年营收预计33.7亿美元，2027年有望跃升至119.8亿美元，增幅约255%。支撑这些预测的，是CoreWeave逾1290亿美元的营收积压订单，以及Nebius超400亿美元的长期合同。 估值层面，CoreWeave当前EV/EBITDA为14.6倍（基于过去十二个月），Nebius的前瞻EV/EBITDA已从过去十二个月的191.4倍大幅压缩至6.4倍。分析师对CoreWeave的平均目标价为131.41美元，对Nebius为286.53美元，较当前股价分别隐含约183%和121%的上行空间。 业务层面也有积极进展。Palantir已将Nebius列为主权AI基础设施的优选合作伙伴，有望打开政府端收入；Nebius在10月完成对Inferize的收购，强化了其推理业务能力。CoreWeave则正在丹麦扩张，并计划从四季度起建设覆盖阿联酋、印度、印度尼西亚、新加坡、澳大利亚、韩国和日本的全球AI网络骨干。 空头逻辑：债务问题可能比营收更重要 然而，依靠债务驱动的增长，其吸引力取决于债务能否以合理条件续期。 CoreWeave在今年8月将资本支出预期上调至350亿至390亿美元，约为其2026年预期营收的三倍。在债券收益率接近困境水平的背景下，市场的核心问题已不再是客户是否需要算力，而是贷款方是否还愿意持续买单。一旦资本支出区间出现被动收窄的迹象，市场可能将其解读为融资受阻，而非主动调整。 Nebius的融资状况相对健康，但也并非无懈可击。其与花旗银行签署的35亿美元优先有担保融资安排期限仅为364天，利率为SOFR加275至350个基点——这意味着用短期资金为长期资产融资，而管理层计划以合同订单为基础推进资产支持融资，需要在一个已明显收紧的市场中落地执行。 此外，CoreWeave的客户集中度风险不容忽视，其主要客户包括微软、OpenAI和Meta。CEO Michael Intrator自IPO以来通过预先安排的交易计划累计减持近10亿美元股票，这一问题可能在当前时机引发治理层面的质疑。Nebius则可能面临有关其前母公司Yandex的追问——后者在俄罗斯数据中心遭受攻击后撤回了2026年业绩预期，尽管两家公司目前已是独立实体。 财报电话会议才是真正的关键 在一个普通季度，小幅超预期加上稳定的业绩指引就已足够。但这不是一个普通季度。 由于两家公司的营收预期均接近共识，数字本身的重要性可能不及管理层在电话会议上的表态。投资者最关注的，是融资条件的最新进展、自由现金流的实现时间表，以及客户基础的多元化程度。市场尤其期待CoreWeave给出一份延伸至2030年的自由现金流路径规划。 利润率的表现同样举足轻重。CoreWeave约58%的EBITDA利润率是其偿债能力论证的核心支柱，Nebius约39%的利润率虽从较低基数快速提升，但任何一家公司的利润率出现滑落，都可能强化"GPU租赁业务的经济性不如增速所呈现的那般诱人"这一判断。 据IG分析，以下几点信号可能成为市场情绪转折的标志：CoreWeave明确350亿至390亿美元资本支出区间并清晰说明资金来源；提供可信的自由现金流转正时间表，最好覆盖至2030年；新增订单显示客户基础超越现有几家超大规模云厂商和AI实验室；Nebius就400亿美元合同订单的资产支持融资安排给出具体细节，并说明364天融资安排的再融资计划；Inferize收购后推理业务的增长证据；以及财报发布后CoreWeave债券收益率和CDS利差的收窄——这或许比股价反应更能说明问题。 Chris Beauchamp在文章中写道： "如果两家公司能够证明资金已经到位、利润率保持稳定，市场或许会认定40%以上的跌幅已经反映了过多的悲观情绪。如果电话会议反而被再融资问题和模糊答案所主导，那么股价腰斩或许是合理定价，而非过度反应。" 风险提示及免责条款
